title: Stretching Micropatterned Cells on a PDMS Membrane
protocol: Cut a piece of PDMS approximately 35 mm x 20 mm from a pre-made sheet.
Remove the top and bottom protective layers of plastic.
Place the PDMS in a plastic Petri dish using tweezers.
Wash the PDMS with 70% ethanol for 5 min on a rotator at 30 oscillations/min.
Dry the surface by flowing air over it.
Illuminate the PDMS with deep UV (λ = 180 nm) for 5 min, about 5 cm from the UV bulbs.
Prepare 200 µl of EDC/NHS solution for each PDMS piece immediately before use.
For 1 ml of MES buffer at pH 6.0, add Sulfo-NHS and EDC as specified.
Transfer PDMS sheets to the lid of the Petri dish that has not been illuminated.
Add EDC/NHS solution and incubate for 15 min at room temperature.
Rinse the PDMS with water.
Add PLL-g-PEG solution (0.5 mg/ml in HEPES, pH 8.6) and incubate from 3 hr to overnight at room temperature.
Rinse the PDMS with water after incubation.
Store passivated PDMS at 4°C for several days if not used immediately.
Take a PDMS sheet and place it on a synthetic quartz photomask bearing the microfeatures for patterning.
Place the PDMS side bearing the PLL-g-PEG facing the chrome side of the photomask.
Illuminate through the photomask for 7 min at a distance from UV bulbs of about 5 cm.
Add water onto the mask + PDMS and peel the PDMS slowly off the mask.
Incubate with fibronectin solution at 50 mg/ml in HEPES buffer at pH 8.6 for 1 hr at room temperature.
Rinse with PBS.
Mount the previously passivated PDMS onto the stretching device.
Attach one side of the PDMS to the fixed part of the stretcher.
Fix the other side to the mobile part of the stretcher without clamping too much of the PDMS sheet.
Cut a rectangle of PDMS (22 mm x 19 mm) in a thick PDMS stab and cut another rectangle inside to create a pool that will retain cells and media.
Add silicone grease under this PDMS pool.
Place the PDMS pool on top of the PDMS sheet to create a medium-retaining pool.
The grease will allow the gliding of the pool over the PDMS sheet during stretching.
Detach the cells from a 50% confluency culture flask with Versene.
Count the cells and resuspend them at a concentration of 200,000 cells/ml.
Mix 1 ml of cell suspension into the pool.
Incubate the cells for 10-30 minutes to allow binding, depending on cell type (RPE-1 cells require 10 min, HeLa cells require 20 min).
Gently flush floating cells with equilibrated medium.
Incubate the cells to spread for at least 2 hours if RPE-1 or 3 hours if HeLa.
Place a coverslip on top of the pool to prevent evaporation and leakage.
Position the device on an inverted microscope for imaging.
Avoid using oil immersion objectives due to focusing issues.
Turn the micrometric screw while adjusting the stage position in x-, y-, and z-axes.
Correct the stage position to counteract PDMS widening and loss of focus.
